# Was the CHU de la Guadeloupe outage a cyberattack?

**Confirmed.** Confirmed. The director says encrypted databases proved a deliberate attack that began Saturday evening, Nov 21. Entry through a hacked IT supplier is Reported. Ransom, data theft and the group are not established.

Incident: CHU de la Guadeloupe hospital cyberattack, Nov 21, 2026. Also reported as Guadeloupe hospital cyberattack and CHU de Guadeloupe plan blanc. First published Nov 22, 2026; last updated Nov 22, 2026, 7:12 PM ET.

> **Not verified: initial investigation only.** Nothing on this page is absolutely confirmed. It is an early look based only on publicly available sources, and it should not be treated as verified fact. Even items labeled "Confirmed" only mean a public source reports them. Made for entertainment using AI. Not endorsed by CHU de la Guadeloupe, ANSSI, any news outlet, government agency, company, or anyone else named.

This is the current answer, not a final verdict.

## The latest

Nov 22, 2026, 7:12 PM ET: **CHU de la Guadeloupe says it was hit by a cyberattack that encrypted data; Confirmed.** New incident page. Sources read: RFI (relaying AFP and La 1ère), France-Antilles Guadeloupe, Guadeloupe La 1ère, RCI Guadeloupe (Tier 2, French). All four report the hospital director's statements, in separate interviews. Main question: Confirmed. Supplier entry: Reported (hedged). Ransom, data theft and group: Not established. A Le Parisien story was seen in search only and not read. No ANSSI or hospital notice read directly. Status monitoring. Privacy check done: no names, bylines, handles or contact details.

## At a glance

- Status: monitoring
- Size: Regional. The hospital says all three of its sites are affected with varying impact, and it has cancelled non-urgent care through Nov 27. It has not given patient numbers.
- Who is affected: Patients and staff of the CHU de la Guadeloupe, in Guadeloupe, France. Urgent care continues; scheduled surgery, consultations and imaging are being cancelled through Nov 27, and patients are told to call the emergency dispatch line before coming.

| Value | What | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| 3 | Hospital sites affected | RFI and RCI; impact varies |
| Nov 27 | Non-urgent care cancelled through | Guadeloupe La 1ère |
| 9 PM | Systems began failing, Nov 21 | RCI, local time |

### Known so far

- The hospital's director says a cyberattack began Saturday evening, Nov 21, and blocked its IT systems and phones.
- Some of the hospital's databases were encrypted and are not accessible.
- The hospital is on paper procedures, with phones, imaging, lab and software disrupted.
- The plan blanc is on and non-urgent care is cancelled through Nov 27.
- The national cybersecurity agency is helping and has told the hospital to expect a long recovery.

### Not known yet

- Whether the attackers really came in through a hacked IT supplier, and which one.
- Whether a ransom was demanded, or any patient data was stolen.
- Who is behind it.
- When systems will be fully back; the hospital hopes for a gradual restart from the end of the week.

## What we checked and did not find

We looked for these and did not find them as of our latest check.

- A statement on the hospital's own site or from the national cybersecurity agency. We read the director's statements through four news outlets (French language).
- The name of the IT supplier said to have been hacked, or any detail of how the attackers used it.
- A ransom note or demand, or any claim of responsibility, in press coverage. We did not look at leak sites, underground forums or trackers.
- Any report that patient data was stolen or published. The director said he could not answer that yet.
- A Le Parisien report (seen in search only, not read).
